data.name: evaluation_description
data.value:
Discover opportunities to optimise activity and workflow YAML grammar and syntax so that expressions can be written in shorthand. Today `when` is the only construct with a compound, language-like expression syntax; the structured `condition` tree is marked LEGACY in its favour yet remains the only available form on actions, reusable fragments and transitions, and technique bindings carry their own separate literal/rename/template deviation forms.

Authoritative current-state sources: the Zod schemas under `src/schema/` (notably `when-expression.ts` and `condition.schema.ts`), the JSON Schemas under `schemas/`, and the 140-file YAML definition corpus under `workflows/`. The `docs/` specifications are in scope as consumers of the grammar that may require updating, not as an authority on it. `grammar/activity.ebnf` and `constraints/activity.als` are placeholders for future work and carry no evidential weight for the current grammar.

The run settles a target grammar covering both activity and workflow definitions and specifies it precisely enough that four formal artifacts could be generated from that specification: `grammar/activity.ebnf` and `constraints/activity.als` brought into alignment, plus new counterparts `grammar/workflow.ebnf` and `constraints/workflow.als`. Those four files are the specification's target consumers, produced by follow-on implementation work; this run does not write them. All output of this run stays within the planning folder.

value.analysis_focus: Evaluate consistency of the two parallel predicate grammars - 281 string when: gates against 109 structured condition: trees with no lowering between them, including the verbatim same four-term predicate written both ways in workflow-authoring/activities/09-validate-and-commit.yaml; the undeclared third grammar in actions[].target (38 uses, 22 with operators) competing with 11 actions[].condition trees on the same verb; the reads/writes asymmetry; and whether constructs appearing at both activity and workflow level are written alike.

Evaluate expressiveness against what authors are forced to restate: the five-line-versus-one-line cost of condition where 75 of 109 are a single leaf and all 86 children restate type: simple; 145 of 410 technique inputs being pure renames with 10 identity passthroughs; required populated on 6 of 525 writes entries; the absence of set-membership against the corpus's a == 'x' || a == 'y' chains; and which of the 15 existing sugar precedents transfer to the un-sugared constructs.

Assess architectural soundness of a shorthand: whether when should desugar into Condition or stay parallel, given two ASTs, two evaluators, two duplicated path resolvers and a single and-combination meeting point in gate-liveness.ts; placement of the parse boundary given the server never evaluates gates and enforcement lives in scripts/; the four-way single source of truth across Zod, generated JSON Schemas, EBNF and Alloy; loader-level sugar present in neither schema; and whether the settled grammar is expressible in EBNF and constrainable in Alloy at all.

Analyse feasibility constraints across the 139-file, 13097-line corpus: when being z.string() so no Zod change catches new syntax, which must instead be taught to tokenize/Parser and to scripts/check-when-expression.ts; JSON Schemas generated from Zod with no regeneration or drift check and already stale; technique.schema.json hand-maintained and already drifted in wording; and migration touching 109 condition blocks, 211 structured technique bindings and 192 graph edges.
Three-pass structural, adversarial and synthesis analysis of the coexisting predicate grammars and the activity/workflow parity question.
Author burden and transferable sugar patterns; desugaring and single-source-of-truth structure; and the migration and enforcement cost of landing a shorthand.

violations.detail: 672 lines against a ~200-line budget written for ~12 findings; 47 consolidated findings from 54 source
